# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes the USDA final rule "Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks" (7 CFR part 2100), published as Federal Register document 2026-13092 on June 29, 2026, and effective July 29, 2026. The rule finalizes the USDA Feedstock Carbon Intensity Calculator (USDA FD-CIC), which quantifies, reports on, and verifies greenhouse gas reduction benefits from low-carbon agricultural practices used to produce biofuel feedstock crops. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The rule "supports the quantification, reporting, and verification of greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction benefits resulting from implementation of low-carbon practices in the production of commodities that are used as biofuel feedstocks in the context of environmental services markets." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* "This rule specifically applies to the production of low- carbon biofuel feedstocks for liquid transportation fuels, which presents a clear environmental services market." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* It applies directly to farm producers of covered feedstock crops (field corn, soybeans, sorghum, spring canola) and to the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities handling reduced-carbon-intensity (reduced-CI) crop. For workspaces that arrange transport or forwarding for agricultural biofuel feedstocks, or that serve clients participating in reduced-CI feedstock or sustainable aviation fuel supply chains, this rule sets the federal documentation and carbon-intensity attestation regime those upstream counterparties must meet. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself, as a freight forwarder rather than a farm producer, aggregator, or intermediary entity, falls within any duty-holder class this rule defines.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** Assess whether any current or prospective client shipping biofuel feedstock crops or reduced-CI processed product relies on USDA FD-CIC certification, since the rule "specifically applies to the production of low- carbon biofuel feedstocks for liquid transportation fuels, which presents a clear environmental services market." *Operational implication:* a forwarder handling reduced-CI feedstock cargo may be asked by shippers to confirm chain-of-custody documentation aligns with the attestation records this rule requires further upstream, even though the forwarder itself is not a named duty-holder in the text. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The rule's obligations attach to farm producers, the first point of aggregation, and intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock supply chain, not to carriers or forwarders. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace activity (e.g., commissioning aggregation, warehousing, or onward distribution of reduced-CI feedstock crop on behalf of a client) brings the workspace within the "first point of aggregation" or "intermediary entities" language the rule uses for its attestation and recordkeeping duties. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Substantive Requirements

**Carbon-intensity quantification and attestation.** Farm producers document field- or management-unit-level carbon intensity using USDA FD-CIC, which "estimates feedstock CIs based on user location, user supplied nutrient management information, and, if applicable, the impact of one or more low-carbon practices." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**MONITORING. Recordkeeping and attestation under penalty of perjury.** The Biofuel Feedstock Report submitted by farm producers, and the attestations required of the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities, must be signed under penalty of perjury: the report must "begin with a statement that the undersigned farm producer certifies the following under penalties of perjury." *Operational implication:* this is a federal false-statement liability mechanism, not a stated civil fine amount; a workspace advising a client on documentation integrity for reduced-CI cargo should treat the attestation as carrying personal legal exposure for the signer, distinct from any commercial penalty. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Third-party verification.** "The final rule requires that entities participating in multiple sustainability certification programs must now provide a third-party verifier with documentation related to their participation in those programs, in addition to programs associated with reduced-CI feedstocks, in order to ensure that environmental benefits (i.e., GHG emissions reductions) are not accounted for in multiple programs." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Record retention.** Nutrient-management records supporting a claimed low-carbon practice "must be kept for 5 years." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Scope limit.** USDA states, verbatim: "While non-GHG ecosystem services are important, they are outside of the scope of this rule." *Analytical inference:* the CI methodology does not extend benefit accounting beyond GHG reduction. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

No exceptions are stated in Sections 2100.001 through 2100.064. No phase-in is stated in Sections 2100.001 through 2100.064; the rule's duties (CI quantification, attestation, verification, retention) apply uniformly from the July 29, 2026 effective date.

Obligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 4.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

The rule does not establish a jurisdictional or producer registration scheme; it operates through the Biofuel Feedstock Report and third-party verification process described above rather than a standing agency registration. *Specific registration or filing deadline not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces whose clients are farm producers, aggregators, or intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock chain: (1) confirm the client's Biofuel Feedstock Report and supporting nutrient-management and manure-application records are retained for the 5-year window this rule sets, and (2) confirm any third-party verifier engagement covers all sustainability certification programs the client participates in, to avoid double-counted GHG benefit claims. *Operational implication:* neither requirement creates a direct forwarding-side system build, since the recordkeeping duty sits with the producer, aggregator, or intermediary, not the carrier or forwarder. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- July 29, 2026: rule effective ("DATES: Effective date: July 29, 2026."). In force as of the export date. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*
- The interim rule preceding this final rule took public comment for 60 days, ending March 18, 2025, and USDA received 114 comments before finalizing the changes reflected in this rule. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Sources

- Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register document 2026-13092, June 29 2026 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes an EPA final rule (40 CFR part 63, Federal Register document 2026-12424, June 22, 2026) that implements a Congressional Review Act (CRA) disapproval of the 2024 amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP) for Rubber Tire Manufacturing. "Under the joint resolution and by operation of the CRA, the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule has no legal force or effect, and the EPA thus is taking this final action to remove the provisions finalized in that rule." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

"On March 5, 2025, the United States House of Representatives passed a joint resolution, H.J. Res. 61, disapproving the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule under the CRA (5 U.S.C. 801 et seq.). The United States Senate passed H.J. Res. 61 on May 6, 2025, and President Donald J. Trump signed it into law as Public Law 119-14 on May 23, 2025." The action "removes the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule's changes to 40 CFR part 63, subpart XXXX, and reverts to the regulatory text in effect immediately prior to the effective date of the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule," i.e., the 2020 Rubber Tire Rule. The subpart states: "You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is a part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* For workspaces that forward cargo for, or serve, rubber tire manufacturers or rubber processing facilities in the United States, this reversion sets the currently binding federal emissions-control baseline those manufacturing clients operate under. *Analytical inference:* the reversion changes only the federal baseline the manufacturing client itself must meet; it creates no new direct duty for a carrier or forwarder handling that client's tire or rubber cargo.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** Confirm with any client that is a rubber tire or rubber processing manufacturer which emission-limitation regime it is currently operating under, since the "first-time air emissions standards for the rubber processing subcategory" introduced by the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule "has no legal force or effect" and the facility instead reverts to the 2020 Rubber Tire Rule's existing-source and new-source limitations. *Operational implication:* a rubber processing subcategory facility that had begun building toward the 2024 standard's first-time limits no longer has a federal compliance obligation to do so under this reverted text; whether any state-level or contractual requirement independently preserves that standard is outside this rule's scope. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The NESHAP obligations run to the owner or operator of the rubber tire manufacturing facility, not to carriers, forwarders, or logistics providers moving tires, tire cord, or rubber feedstock. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace activity constitutes "owning or operating" a covered rubber tire manufacturing facility as the subpart defines it; absent that, the workspace sits outside this rule's direct duty-holder class.

# Substantive Requirements

**Reverted existing-source compliance deadline.** The reinstated 2020 Rubber Tire Rule text requires that "if you have an existing affected source, you must comply with the emission limitations for existing sources no later than July 11, 2005," and that an area source that grows into major-source status "must be in compliance with existing source emission limitations no later than 3 years after the date on which the area source became a major source." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

**Applicability determination.** "You must determine which subpart applies to your source and you must be in compliance with the applicable subpart by the compliance date of that subpart." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

**Rubber processing subcategory limits removed.** The 2024 Rubber Tire Rule's rubber-processing-subcategory limits, described in the captured text as promulgating "air emissions standards for the rubber processing subcategory of the rubber tire manufacturing source category" for the first time, are removed by this action and do not currently bind covered facilities. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

*Specific penalty or enforcement provision not available from primary sources as of the export date; the captured text addresses the CRA revocation mechanics and the reverted 2020 emission-limitation text, not Clean Air Act enforcement remedies.* *Operational implication:* because the duty holder is the manufacturing facility, not the forwarder, none of these reverted requirements create a direct compliance obligation for the workspace itself, only a client-posture question to track.

**Applicability determination duty.** "You must determine which subpart applies to your source and you must be in compliance with the applicable subpart by the compliance date of that subpart." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

**Area-source growth deadline.** An area source that grows into major-source status "must be in compliance with existing source emission limitations no later than 3 years after the date on which the area source became a major source." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

**New/reconstructed-source exception.** The reinstated text provides that a new or reconstructed affected source complies "except as provided in Sec. Sec. 63.5982(b)(4) and 63.5981(b)(1)". *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

**Major/minor-source threshold carve-out.** "You are not subject to this subpart if the affected source at your rubber tire manufacturing facility meets either of the conditions described in paragraph (b)(1) or (2) of this section." *Analytical inference:* a facility below the major-source HAP threshold, or whose primary product is regulated under another subpart, falls outside this subpart's duty-holder class entirely. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

No scope limits are stated in Sections 63.5981 through 63.6015; applicability there is framed as "subject to"/"not subject to" this subpart, captured above, rather than as a scope-limit clause. No phase-in is stated in Sections 63.5981 through 63.6015; the reinstated existing-source and new-source deadlines apply on the fixed dates stated above, not a stepped multi-year schedule.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reverted 2020 text carries its own recordkeeping and reporting procedures ("ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with the general requirements of Sec. 63.10(c), (e)(1), and (e)(2)(i)"), which the owner or operator "shall keep... on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* *Specific registration filing format or agency portal not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces supporting rubber tire or rubber processing manufacturing clients: (1) confirm which subpart and compliance date governs the client's specific affected source now that the 2024 rubber-processing-subcategory standard has been removed, and (2) confirm the client's recordkeeping retention covers the life of the affected source as the reinstated text requires. *Operational implication:* this is a client compliance-posture verification, not a direct system build for the forwarder, since the duty holder is the manufacturing facility. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- March 5, 2025: U.S. House of Representatives passes H.J. Res. 61 disapproving the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule. In force as of the export date. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- May 6, 2025: U.S. Senate passes H.J. Res. 61. In force as of the export date. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- May 23, 2025: President signs H.J. Res. 61 into law as Public Law 119-14. In force as of the export date. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- November 29, 2024: this final rule's effective date, per the CRA's retroactive-nullification treatment of the disapproved 2024 Rubber Tire Rule ("This final rule is effective November 29, 2024."). In force as of the export date. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- June 22, 2026: EPA publishes this final rule removing the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule's regulatory text. In force as of the export date. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# Sources

- Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register document 2026-12424, June 22 2026 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023, which publishes an updated user's guide setting out the steps organisations need to take to participate in the EU eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS), adopted under Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The Decision "repeal[s]" the prior guide decision: "Article 2 Decision 2013/131/EU is repealed." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

EMAS is established by "Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the voluntary participation by organisations in a EU eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS)." Participation is voluntary, not a binding compliance obligation. This Decision itself operates at Member State level: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, as an organisation potentially seeking EMAS registration for its own environmental management system, would be treated as an "organisation" under Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 for registration purposes; this Decision's own text does not itself impose an obligation on private operators.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**COMPETITIVE EDGE.** Assess whether EMAS registration is worth pursuing as a voluntary sustainability credential, since the published guide is intended so that "interested organisations should receive additional information and guidance about the steps needed to participate in EMAS." *Operational implication:* EMAS registration is a differentiator a workspace can cite to clients in cargo verticals with strong environmental scrutiny (e.g., fine art, luxury goods, film and TV logistics), but registration is voluntary and this Decision creates no compliance deadline or penalty exposure for non-participation. *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Decision's addressees are the Member States, who administer EMAS through national competent bodies and environmental verifiers: "the environmental verifier as referred to in Article 2(20) of the EMAS Regulation is... a conformity assessment b[ody]," and organisations may "contact the competent bodies in the countries where the organisations concerned are based." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* A workspace considering registration would engage its national competent body directly; the workspace is not a duty-holder under this Decision itself.

# Substantive Requirements

**Publication of the guide.** "The user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in Union eco-management and audit scheme as set out in the Annex is hereby published." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* The guide's substantive content (environmental review, environmental policy, environmental programme, management system set-up) is voluntary implementation guidance for an organisation pursuing EMAS registration, not a binding requirement imposed by this Decision on external parties.

*Specific compliance deadline, effective date, and penalty provision not available from primary sources as of the export date: the captured Decision text publishes guidance and repeals a prior guide Decision, and states no entry-into-force clause, no deadline binding external organisations, and no penalty or sanction provision.*

**Article 1 -- publication of the guide.** "The user’s guide setting out the steps needed to participate in Union eco-management and audit scheme as set out in the Annex is hereby published." *Analytical inference:* this is a publication act, not a duty imposed on any private operator. *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

**Verification-frequency exemption for small organisations.** "For small organisations, Article 7 of the EMAS Regulation provides for exemptions to the frequency of verifications for renewal, allowing them to be carried out every 4 years, with an intermediate one every 2 years." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

**Hazardous-waste site exception.** The guide's environmental-statement checklist covers "sites subject to hazardous waste management legislation, except for producers of hazardous waste in small quantities which are subject to national and/or regional exemptions." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

**Environmental-statement renewal cadence.** "Every 3 years (with the exemption for small companies every 4 years), the environmental statement must be completely renewed, along with the EMAS registration to be validated by the environmental verifier and submitted to the competent body." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

**Global EMAS scope of registration.** "EMAS is applicable inside and outside the EU (‘global EMAS’) to sites in various EU and non-EU countries that can be included in the scope of registration." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

**Scope-of-registration factors.** In defining the scope of registration, "the organisation must consider: ✓ external and internal issues. ✓ compliance obligations. ✓ its organisational units, functions, and physical boundaries. ✓ its activities, products, and services. ✓ its authority and ability to exercise control and influence." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 3 or the published Annex; the renewal and verification cadences captured above are fixed, recurring cycles, not a stepped multi-year threshold.

Obligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 6.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Registration under EMAS is voluntary and administered by Member State competent bodies rather than by a jurisdiction-wide filing deadline stated in this Decision. *Specific registration deadline not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

# Operational System Requirements

For a workspace evaluating EMAS registration: (1) contact the national competent body in the relevant Member State to scope the environmental review, environmental policy, and environmental management system steps the published guide describes, and (2) engage an accredited environmental verifier as defined in Article 2(20) of the EMAS Regulation. *Operational implication:* these are voluntary program-entry steps, not deadline-bound compliance obligations, so there is no gap-from-baseline analysis of the kind a mandatory regulation would require. *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 3 November 2023: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 adopted, repealing Decision 2013/131/EU. In force as of the export date (no entry-into-force clause or amendment identified in the captured text). *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

# Sources

- Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes a Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 (2022/C 77/02) instructing the central administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter corrected national allocation tables of free EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) allowances for ten Member States, "Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden," into the log. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

"Member States submitted to the Commission the list of installations under their territory pursuant to Article 11(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council," the directive establishing the EU ETS. The Decision instructs entry into the Union Transaction Log of "corrected national allocation tables... for the transitional free allocation of emission allowances for the period from 2021 to 2025." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).* This is a technical, administrative EU ETS registry correction affecting the free-allowance entitlement of specific stationary industrial installations in the ten named Member States, not an obligation reaching the workspace directly; it belongs to the background EU ETS allocation machinery that shapes the carbon-cost environment those installations, and any freight that serves them, operate in.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** No workspace-facing deadline or obligation is stated in this Decision's own text; the corrective action runs between the Commission, the named Member States, and the central administrator of the registry. *Operational implication:* for workspaces with cargo verticals touching EU ETS-covered industrial installations (e.g., high-value automotive manufacturing supply chains in the affected Member States), this correction has no direct compliance step for the forwarder, but it is one input into the free-allocation baseline those installations' own carbon cost exposure is measured against. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Decision's single operative article instructs only the central administrator: "the central administrator of the European Union Transaction Log is instructed to enter the corrected national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).* No addressee clause naming Member States, economic operators, or private parties was located in the captured text; the workspace sits entirely outside the Decision's operative scope.

# Substantive Requirements

The corrections addressed by this Decision are installation-level data fixes: for example, "Sweden notified corrections to its national allocation table by letter dated 22 November 2021." The correction concerned "reported values for electricity consumption that are used for calculating the electricity" component of free allocation, and Finland "corrected the reported heat values and therefore the historical activity levels" after several installations "reported wrong heat balance between eligible and non-eligible heat for free allocation." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).* These are registry-accuracy corrections to the transitional free-allocation calculation for named installations, not new obligations.

*Specific effective date, compliance deadline, and penalty provision not available from primary sources as of the export date: the captured text is a single-article administrative instruction to the Central Administrator, states no entry-into-force clause, no deadline binding an external party, and no penalty or sanction provision.*

**Approval-with-exception recital.** "The Commission raised no objections to the lists of installations covered by Directive 2003/87/EC as submitted by Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden, except as set out in Article 1 and Annexes of that Decision." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

**Croatia registry-exclusion correction.** "Installation HR-205907 was included by mistake in the national allocation table as it was excluded from ETS pursuant to Article 27." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

**Finland heat-balance correction.** Finland "corrected the reported heat values and therefore the historical activity levels" after several installations "reported wrong heat balance between eligible and non-eligible heat for free allocation." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

No scope limits are stated in Article 1. No phase-in is stated in Article 1; the corrections apply to the fixed 2021-to-2025 allocation period stated above, not a stepped schedule.

Shortfall: the remaining per-country notification recitals (Belgium, Germany, Greece, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland) restate the same notify-and-correct pattern already captured for Sweden, Finland, and Croatia; no distinct obligation type remains unextracted in a single-article registry-correction instruction.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 4.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Registration and reporting under the EU ETS free-allocation regime runs through the national allocation tables the ten Member States submitted under Directive 2003/87/EC Article 11(1); this Decision is the Commission's instruction to record the corrected versions of those tables, not a new filing requirement. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

# Operational System Requirements

No workspace-facing operational system build is indicated by this Decision's text; the corrections apply to the free-allocation calculations of named EU ETS installations administered by the ten Member States and the Commission. *No operational system requirement identified for the workspace as of the export date.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 17 December 2021: Commission adopts the Decision instructing entry of the corrected national allocation tables ("Done at Brussels, 17 December 2021"). In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*
- 22 November 2021: Sweden notifies its national allocation table corrections by letter, addressed by this Decision. In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

# Sources

- Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 (2022/C 77/02), European Commission, OJ C 77/19, published 2022 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02)

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), the consolidated framework requiring an environmental permit for regulated facilities including waste operations, installations, mobile plant, water discharge activities, groundwater activities, radioactive substances activities, and medium combustion plants in England and Wales. "These Regulations may be cited as the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 and come into force 21 days after the day on which these Regulations are made." *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

"A person must not, except under and to the extent authorised by an environmental permit... (a) operate a regulated facility, or (b) cause or knowingly permit a water discharge activity or groundwater activity." "These Regulations extend to England and Wales only." *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.* For workspaces operating or contracting UK-based warehousing, cross-dock, waste-transfer, or storage facilities in England and Wales that carry out a "waste operation" ("the direct or indirect release of substances, vibrations, heat or noise from individual or diffuse sources related to the operation into the air, water or land") or that run on-site combustion plant (e.g., backup generators, boilers) meeting the "medium combustion plant" definition, this Regulation sets the permitting gate that must be satisfied before operating. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace-controlled site (warehouse, depot, storage facility) meets the definition of a "regulated facility" or carries out a "medium combustion plant" activity as this Regulation defines those terms.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**ACTION REQUIRED.** Verify environmental permit coverage for any England/Wales facility the workspace operates or contracts that runs a regulated waste operation, water discharge activity, or medium combustion plant, since operating without one is an offence: "It is an offence for a person to... contravene regulation 12(1)." *Operational implication:* an unpermitted regulated facility, or one operating outside its permit conditions, exposes the operator to criminal liability under regulation 38, not merely a civil compliance gap. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The duty to hold and comply with an environmental permit falls on "the operator" of the regulated facility or the person who causes or knowingly permits a water discharge or groundwater activity. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, as freight forwarder, is itself "the operator" of any England/Wales site in scope, or whether that duty sits with a warehousing/3PL subcontractor whose permit status the workspace should verify contractually before routing cargo through the site.

# Substantive Requirements

**Permit requirement.** "A person must not, except under and to the extent authorised by an environmental permit... operate a regulated facility, or... cause or knowingly permit a water discharge activity or groundwater activity." *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

**Offences.** "It is an offence for a person to... contravene regulation 12(1), or... knowingly cause or knowingly permit the contravention of regulation 12(1)(a)," and separately "It is an offence for a person to fail to comply with or to contravene an environmental permit condition." A person guilty of an offence under regulation 38 is liable "on conviction on indictment to a fine or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years, or to both." *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

**Notices and withdrawal.** The enforcing authority "must" act on a compliance notice served on the operator "and... must withdraw a notice when satisfied that the steps specified in it have been taken," establishing a defined remediation-and-close-out process once a notice issues. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

**Medium combustion plant cutoff.** An "existing medium combustion plant" is one "put into operation before 20th December 2018, or... for which an environmental permit was granted before 19th December 2017, provided that the plant is put into operation" by a further specified date; plant falling outside this cutoff is treated as new and subject to the current permitting regime rather than the existing-plant transitional provisions. *Analytical inference:* these permitting, offence, and enforcement provisions run to facility operators and permit holders directly; a forwarder arranging transport to or from a permitted site is not itself an operator or permit holder under this instrument absent a separate operational role there. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

**Medium combustion plant phase-in schedule.** "Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply in relation to the operation of a medium combustion plant, mobile medium combustion plant or a specified generator comprising— (a) a new medium combustion plant, before 20th December 2018; (b) an existing medium combustion plant with a rated thermal input greater than 5 megawatts, before 1st January 2024; (c) an existing medium combustion plant with a rated thermal input of less than or equal to 5 megawatts, before 1st January 2029;" *Analytical inference:* this is a stepped, three-tier phase-in by plant size, not a single cutoff. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

**Public participation scope and exception.** "Public participation: scope E+W 5. —(1) Paragraph 6 applies to every application for the grant of an environmental permit except an application in relation to— (a) mobile plant, (b) a radioactive substances activity described in paragraph 11(5) of Part 2 of Schedule 23" *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

No per-year step-up beyond the three dated tiers above is stated in the medium-combustion-plant phase-in; the trajectory is captured in this brief's metadata.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Environmental permits are applied for and held under the regime this Regulation establishes rather than through a separate standalone registration filing; *specific application form, portal, or filing-fee detail not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces operating or contracting England/Wales sites in scope: (1) confirm the site's environmental permit is current and covers the specific regulated facility class or water discharge/groundwater activity conducted there, (2) for any on-site combustion plant, confirm whether it is treated as "existing" under the 20 December 2018 cutoff or falls under the current new-plant permitting standard, and (3) build a contractual verification step for any subcontracted UK warehousing or waste-handling site to confirm permit compliance before cargo is routed through it. *Operational implication:* the compliance gap between an unverified subcontractor site and this Regulation's permit requirement is a workspace exposure even where the workspace itself does not hold the permit. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

**compliance_deadline.** The export's forward-events ledger records a compliance-deadline milestone tied to "20th December 2018" -- the medium-combustion-plant phase-in cutoff captured above (new-plant compliance no later than 20th December 2018), also carried on the Confirmed Regulatory Timeline below. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

In force as of the export date. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

- 7 April 2019: regulation 39 (Penalties and enforcement undertakings) inserted/amended by The Environmental Protection (Miscellaneous Amendments) (England and Wales) Regulations 2018 (S.I. 2018/1227). In force as of the export date. *Source: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 2016/1154), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/1154.*

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015, which establishes the common noise assessment methods (the CNOSSOS-EU methodology) Member States must use under the Environmental Noise Directive 2002/49/EC. *Analytical inference:* the scope language below describes the methodology's technical application to infrastructure noise sources; it does not by itself create a duty running to a forwarder or carrier. "Annex II to Directive 2002/49/EC is replaced by the text set out in the Annex to this Directive." The Annex's calculation method "applies to industrial infrastructures and land transport infrastructures. It therefore applies in particular to road and railway infrastructures. Aircraft transport is included in the scope of the method only for the noise produced during ground operations and excludes take-off and landing." *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Under Directive 2002/49/EC, "Member States shall ensure that strategic noise maps are made... no later than 30 June 2007 and 30 June 2012 and thereafter reviewed, and revised if necessary, at least every 5 years," and "Directive 2002/49/EC provides for action plans to be based on strategic noise maps." *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.* This Directive standardizes how those maps and the resulting action plans are calculated for roads, railways, industrial sites, and aircraft ground operations. For workspaces operating transport, warehousing, or event-logistics activity near mapped noise-sensitive infrastructure (major roads, railway lines, airports, industrial estates) in EU Member States, the strategic noise maps and action plans this methodology feeds can drive locally imposed operating restrictions (curfews, routing limits, noise-abatement procedures). *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any specific local noise action plan derived from this methodology imposes an operating restriction on a workspace-controlled site or route.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** Track whether the competent authority for any airport, major road, or railway corridor the workspace regularly uses for time-sensitive cargo (e.g., live-events touring, film and TV production logistics) has published or updated a noise action plan under the CNOSSOS-EU methodology, since national transposition of this common assessment method was required "by 31 December 2018 at the latest." *Operational implication:* a newly adopted or revised noise action plan can introduce or tighten night-time movement restrictions at airports or road corridors relevant to time-critical, high-value cargo scheduling, even though this Directive itself imposes no direct obligation on carriers or forwarders. *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive's own obligations run to Member States: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." It requires Member State authorities to "bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive," not workspace-level compliance. *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.* *Analytical inference:* any operational consequence for the workspace arrives indirectly, through a Member State's own noise action plan or airport/road operating restriction, not through a direct duty this Directive creates for carriers or forwarders.

# Substantive Requirements

**Scope of the calculation method.** "The method of calculation described in this document applies to industrial infrastructures and land transport infrastructures... in particular to road and railway infrastructures," with aircraft transport "included in the scope of the method only for the noise produced during ground operations and excludes take-off and landing." *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

**Transposition obligation.** "Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 31 December 2018 at the latest. They shall forthwith communicate to the Commission the text of those provisions." *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

**Strategic noise mapping cadence.** Strategic noise maps under the parent Directive 2002/49/EC must be produced "no later than 30 June 2007 and 30 June 2012 and thereafter reviewed, and revised if necessary, at least every 5 years," feeding the action plans this common methodology standardizes. *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

*Specific penalty, sanction, or enforcement provision not available from primary sources as of the export date: this Directive is a technical implementing measure addressed to Member States and states no penalty provision binding an operator, carrier, or forwarder.* *Analytical inference:* the transposition and mapping-cadence duties above run to Member State authorities, not to workspace operators, so no direct workspace filing obligation arises from this Directive's text.

**Octave-band calculation exception.** "Calculations are performed in octave bands for road traffic, railway traffic and industrial noise, except for the railway noise source sound power, that uses third octave bands." *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

**Partial-cover scope exclusion.** "Partial covers and obstacles sloping, when modelled, more than 15° in relation to the vertical are out of the scope of this calculation method." *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

No additional per-year step-up beyond the parent Directive's mapping-and-review cadence above (2007, 2012, then every 5 years) is stated in this Directive's own Annex; the trajectory is captured in this brief's metadata.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Member States "shall forthwith communicate to the Commission the text of" the transposing national provisions once adopted; this is a Member-State-to-Commission reporting duty, not a workspace-facing filing. *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces with recurring time-sensitive movements near mapped noise-sensitive infrastructure: (1) monitor the relevant airport, road, or rail authority's published noise action plan for movement-window or curfew changes, and (2) build lead-time buffers into scheduling for cargo (e.g., live-events staging, film production equipment) that depends on off-peak or night-time transport near noise-restricted corridors. *Operational implication:* since the Directive creates no direct workspace duty, this is a monitoring-and-scheduling control rather than a compliance build. *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

# Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**compliance_deadline.** The export's forward-events ledger records the parent Directive's strategic-noise-mapping cadence, tied to "30 June 2007" -- the first mapping round, followed by a second round "30 June 2012" and review "at least every 5 years" thereafter (captured in Substantive Requirements above and on the Confirmed Regulatory Timeline). *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 19 May 2015: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 adopted. In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*
- "This Directive shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*
- 31 December 2018: deadline for Member States to bring national transposing measures into force. In force as of the export date (deadline passed). *Source: Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015 establishing common noise assessment methods according to Directive 2002/49/EC, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996.*

# Sources

- Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 of 19 May 2015, European Commission, OJ L 168, 1.7.2015 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015L0996

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes the Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), a broad UK primary Act covering hydrogen production revenue support, carbon capture and storage licensing, gas and electricity economic regulation, and related energy-transition infrastructure. "This Act may be cited as the Energy Act 2023." *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.* Given the Act's breadth, this document is scoped to the provisions the captured text grounds: hydrogen production revenue support contracts and the hydrogen levy, carbon storage licensee notification duties to the North Sea Transition Authority (OGA), and the licence-holder financial penalty regime; other parts of the Act are outside this document's grounded scope.

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Act empowers the Secretary of State to make "revenue support regulations" funding "hydrogen production revenue support contracts," recovered through a hydrogen levy charged to "GB gas shippers" and "Northern Ireland gas shippers": "a description so specified may not include persons other than" (a) "GB gas shippers" or (b) "Northern Ireland gas shippers." It also creates licensee duties in the carbon storage regime: "a licensee, and... an exploration operator under a carbon storage licence... must appoint an individual to act as an information and samples coordinator, and notify the OGA of that individual's name and contact details." For workspaces engaged in hydrogen or alternative-fuel supply chains, or providing logistics for carbon capture, usage and storage (CCUS) project equipment and materials, this Act sets the funding and licensing framework those upstream counterparties operate under. The Act applies to activities in "the territorial sea adjacent to the United Kingdom," covering offshore carbon storage and gas activity. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's own logistics or forwarding role for CCUS project equipment, materials, or personnel could bring it within the Act's licensee or market-participant duty classes rather than remaining an unaffected third-party carrier. *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**COST ALERT.** Assess whether any client that is a GB or Northern Ireland gas shipper is exposed to hydrogen levy pass-through costs, since the levy is recovered from those shipper classes to fund hydrogen production revenue support contracts. *Operational implication:* a gas-shipper client's hydrogen levy exposure can flow into downstream energy pricing that affects freight and warehousing operating costs where gas is a direct input, though the specific pass-through mechanism to any individual workspace client requires client-specific data. *Analytical inference:* effect on cost of gas-dependent operations requires carrier-specific and shipper-specific data. *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Act's duty holders are gas shippers (for the hydrogen levy), and licensees or exploration operators under a carbon storage licence (for the OGA notification duty); the workspace, as freight forwarder, does not fall within either duty-holder class on the captured text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace activity constitutes acting as a "GB gas shipper" or holding a "carbon storage licence" as the Act defines those terms; absent that, the workspace's exposure is indirect, through client relationships with covered gas shippers or carbon storage licensees.

# Substantive Requirements

**Hydrogen levy recovery.** "Any sum that— (a) a relevant market participant is required by virtue of revenue support regulations to pay to a hydrogen levy administrator, and (b) has not been paid by the date on which it is required by virtue of revenue support regulations to be paid, may be recovered from the relevant market participant by the hydrogen levy administrator as a civil debt due to it." Levy-payer eligibility is restricted to "GB gas shippers" and "Northern Ireland gas shippers." *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

**Financial penalty right of appeal.** "Provision made by virtue of subsection (3) (d) for the imposition of a financial penalty must include provision for a right of appeal against the imposition of the penalty." *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

**Carbon storage information coordinator duty.** A licensee or carbon storage exploration operator "must appoint an individual to act as an information and samples coordinator, and notify the OGA of that individual's name and contact details," and "must comply with subsection (1) within a reasonable period after... the date on which this section comes into force... or... becoming a relevant person." *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

**Licence-holder penalty cap.** "The maximum amount of penalty that may be imposed on a licence holder in respect of a contravention may not exceed 10 per cent of the licence holder’s turnover." *Analytical inference:* the levy, appeal, coordinator, and penalty-cap duties above run to gas shippers, licensees, and market participants; a forwarder without one of those regulatory roles carries no direct duty under these provisions, only a client-posture question to track. *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

**Territorial scope of the Part 1 prohibition.** "Territorial scope of prohibition U.K. Section 2 (1) applies to activities in, above or below— (a) the territorial sea adjacent to the United Kingdom, or (b) waters in a Gas Importation and Storage Zone (within the meaning given by section 1 of the Energy Act 2008), as it applies to activities in the United Kingdom." *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

**Prosecution-consent exception.** "No proceedings may be instituted in England and Wales in respect of an offence under this section except by or on behalf of the Secretary of State or the economic regulator." *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

No phase-in is stated in Sections 2 to 5 and 70 to 74; the net zero review date already on the Confirmed Regulatory Timeline is a single statutory review point, not a phased threshold.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Economic-regulator reporting includes "a summary of final and provisional orders made and penalties imposed by the economic regulator during the year" as part of the annual transport-and-storage (T&S) report. Carbon storage licensees separately notify the OGA of their appointed information and samples coordinator, as above. *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces with clients that are gas shippers or carbon storage licensees: (1) confirm the client's hydrogen levy payment status to the levy administrator, since unpaid sums are recoverable from the relevant market participant, and (2) for carbon storage clients, confirm an information and samples coordinator has been appointed and notified to the OGA within the statutory reasonable period after becoming a relevant person. *Operational implication:* neither duty creates a direct system build for the forwarder, since the duty holders are the gas shipper or the licensee, not the carrier. *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- "The provisions of this Act come into force on such day or days as the Secretary of State may by regulations appoint," with specified provisions in force at Royal Assent or by later commencement regulations, for example: "S. 70 in force at 26.12.2023, see s. 334(3)(b)". In force as of the export date for commenced provisions. *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*
- 31 December 2040 and each five-year anniversary is the "relevant date" for a net zero-related statutory review; where the Secretary of State decides not to repeal a relevant provision, a statement must be published "no later than 3 months after that date explaining why not." *Analytical inference:* the review-and-explain duty binds the Secretary of State, not the workspace or its clients directly. *Source: Energy Act 2023 (c. 52), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/52.*
