# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes the Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), the UK Act that established the Environment Agency and the Scottish Environment Protection Agency, created the contaminated land regime, and made further provision for National Parks and pollution control. The long title states the Act is "to provide for the establishment of... bodies... to make provision with respect to contaminated land and abandoned mines; to make further provision in relation to National Parks; to make further provision for the control of pollution, the conservation of natural resources and the conservation or enhancement of the environment." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.* Given the Act's breadth and long amendment history, this document is scoped to the provisions the captured text grounds: contaminated land special sites, National Park authority general powers, offence and penalty provisions, and the Act's commencement and extent clauses.

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Act's contaminated land regime empowers a local authority, and in some cases the Environment Agency, to identify and remediate contaminated land: "If, in a case where a local authority has served a remediation notice, the contaminated land in question becomes a special site, the appropriate Agency may adopt the remediation notice." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.* For workspaces that own, lease, or operate UK warehousing, depot, or storage sites, this regime can attach remediation liability and cost exposure to land found to be contaminated, independent of when the contamination occurred. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, as occupier or operator of a specific UK site, would be the "appropriate person" under Part IIA of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 (as the contaminated land regime the Environment Act 1995 inserted) bearing remediation cost for that site.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**ACTION REQUIRED.** Confirm contaminated-land search and due-diligence coverage for any UK warehouse, depot, or storage site the workspace owns, leases, or is evaluating, given the special-sites and remediation-notice regime this Act's contaminated land provisions create. *Operational implication:* remediation notice liability attaches to land, not to a specific tenancy term, so a site's contaminated-land status should be checked before committing to a new lease or acquisition, not only at the point of an active notice. *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The duty to remediate contaminated land runs to the "appropriate person" as Part IIA defines that term (generally the polluter, or in default the current owner or occupier), and enforcement runs through the local authority or, for a special site, "the appropriate Agency." *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's occupation of a specific site (as tenant, licensee, or owner) would place it within the appropriate-person class for that site should contamination be identified.

# Substantive Requirements

**Special sites and remediation notices.** "If, in a case where a local authority has served a remediation notice, the contaminated land in question becomes a special site, the appropriate Agency may adopt the remediation notice and, if it does so... it shall give notice of its decision to adopt the remediation notice to the appropriate person and to the local authority." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

**National Park authority general powers.** An English National Park authority "may do anything it considers appropriate for the purposes of the carrying out of any of its functions," and that power "confers power... to do it anywhere in the United Kingdom or elsewhere," subject to a boundary rule that the power "does not enable an English National Park authority to do anything which it is unable to do by virtue of a pre-commencement limitation." A "pre-commencement limitation" includes a restriction "contained in an Act passed no later than the end of the Session in which the Cities and Local Government Devolution Act 2016 is passed." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.* *Operational implication:* workspaces operating logistics or event-transport activity within or adjacent to an English National Park should confirm whether a National Park authority byelaw or access restriction constitutes such a pre-commencement limitation on the authority's own general-power expansion, since that shapes what the authority may newly regulate versus what remains fixed by pre-existing law.

**Offence for obstruction or false statement.** "A person commits an offence if the person... fails without reasonable excuse to give any assistance that a relevant official reasonably requests in the exercise of a power" or "otherwise intentionally obstructs a relevant official in exercising one of those powers." A related offence for making a false statement to an authority is "liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

**Water-industry-interference offence penalty.** "The person guilty of the offence is liable— (a) on summary conviction, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding the general limit in a magistrates’ court or to a fine, or both; (b) on conviction on indictment, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or to a fine, or both." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

**Apportionment exception between contaminated-land parties.** "No remediation notice shall require person B to do anything by way of remediation to that other land in consequence of the apparent acts or omissions of person A, except to the extent that person B caused or knowingly permitted the escape." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

**Scope of a review, assessment, or action plan.** Regulations may make provision "for or in connection with" "the scope or form of a review or assessment" and "the scope, content or form of an action plan." *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

No phase-in is stated in Sections 78 to 78Q and 65A to 65D; the commencement and remediation provisions grounded above attach on fixed trigger events (notice service, special-site designation), not a phased numeric schedule.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Remediation notices and special-site adoption decisions are administered directly between the local authority, the appropriate Agency, and the appropriate person on a site-by-site basis rather than through a standing jurisdiction-wide filing regime. *Specific registration or filing deadline not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces with UK land holdings or leases: (1) commission a contaminated-land search before acquiring or renewing a lease on a warehouse, depot, or storage site, and (2) build an escalation path for responding to a local authority information request or inspection under the Act's enforcement powers, given the obstruction offence attaches personal criminal liability up to two years' imprisonment on indictment for the most serious enforcement-obstruction offences under related provisions. *Operational implication:* this due diligence step protects against inheriting remediation cost exposure through an unreviewed site acquisition or lease renewal. *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- "This Act shall come into force on such day as the Secretary of State may specify by order made by statutory instrument," with different days appointed for different provisions (Part III came into force at the end of the period of two months beginning with the day the Act was passed, subject to specified exceptions). In force as of the export date for commenced provisions. *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*
- 28 January 2016 (specified purposes) / 28 March 2016 (remaining purposes): sections 65A to 65D (English National Park authority general powers) inserted by the Cities and Local Government Devolution Act 2016. In force as of the export date. *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*
- "This Act shall not extend to Northern Ireland," except for specified sections and amendments to named Acts. In force as of the export date. *Source: Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government (legislation.gov.uk), as amended. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25.*

# Sources

- Environment Act 1995 (c. 25), UK Government, legislation.gov.uk, as amended (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/25

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025, which establishes the default values CBAM declarants use to determine embedded emissions in goods (other than electricity), indirect embedded emissions, and embedded emissions in imported electricity, under the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). "Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 requires the use of default values for determining embedded emissions in goods other than electricity and in imported electricity, and for determining indirect embedded emissions." *Analytical inference:* this default-value obligation runs to CBAM declarants determining embedded emissions; a forwarder is relevant only insofar as it assists a declarant client with the underlying cargo data, not as a declarant itself absent that role. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

"Where the embedded emissions in imported goods are determined on the basis of default values in accordance with Article 7(2), point (b), of Regulation (EU) 2023/956, the default values laid down in Annex I to this Regulation shall be used." A derogation also applies to precursor materials: "where a country of production cannot be identified for a precursor, the default values laid down in Annex IV shall be used." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.* "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.* For workspaces forwarding or brokering customs clearance for CBAM-covered goods (cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, hydrogen, and electricity) imported into the EU, this Regulation supplies the fallback emissions figures an importer or authorised CBAM declarant must use when actual supplier-level emissions data is unavailable. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, or a specific client it forwards for, is itself the importer or authorised CBAM declarant responsible for applying these default values, as opposed to a party merely arranging transport.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**COST ALERT.** Confirm with any importer or customs-broker client handling CBAM-covered cargo whether their embedded-emissions declarations rely on these default values or on actual supplier data, since default values apply "where the embedded emissions in imported goods are determined on the basis of default values." *Operational implication:* a client using default values (as opposed to actual, typically lower, verified supplier emissions) may face a higher CBAM certificate cost exposure than one with verified data, which can affect quoted landed cost and margin conversations with the client. *Analytical inference:* the magnitude of that cost difference for a specific shipment requires product-and-route-specific data. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The duty to determine and declare embedded emissions, whether by default values or actual values, sits with the importer or authorised CBAM declarant under Regulation (EU) 2023/956, not with the forwarder arranging carriage. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's role in a given transaction (freight forwarder, customs broker, or NVOCC) brings it within the "authorised CBAM declarant" duty-holder class Regulation (EU) 2023/956 defines, or whether that duty sits entirely with the importer client.

# Substantive Requirements

**Default values for imported goods.** "Where the embedded emissions in imported goods are determined on the basis of default values in accordance with Article 7(2), point (b), of Regulation (EU) 2023/956, the default values laid down in Annex I to this Regulation shall be used." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

**Precursor derogation.** "Where a country of production cannot be identified for a precursor, the default values laid down in Annex IV shall be used." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

**Scheduled revision.** The default values set by this Regulation are not fixed indefinitely: "It shall be revised in 2027 at the latest." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.* *Analytical inference:* importer and forwarder clients relying on these default values should expect a revised default-value set to apply from the 2027 revision, which can change declared emissions and certificate cost calculations for the same goods without any change in the underlying supply chain.

*Specific penalty, sanction, or enforcement provision not available from primary sources as of the export date: this implementing Regulation sets default emissions values and states no penalty provision of its own; CBAM's own penalty regime sits in the parent Regulation (EU) 2023/956, not in the captured text.*

**Electricity carve-out from Annex I.** "ANNEX I Default values for goods imported into the customs territory of the Union, except for electricity" -- electricity default values are set separately in Annex III. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

**Gradual mark-up phase-in.** "To avoid immediate disproportionate impacts on prices of goods, and to give economic operators time to adapt, the mark-up should be gradually phased-in. This phase-in, is also necessary as the number of verifiers may increase in the first years following the end of the transition period, in particular in 2026." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 3; the Regulation instead frames applicability through the goods, electricity, and precursor categories captured above.

Obligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 5.

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Default values apply within the CBAM declaration process the parent Regulation (EU) 2023/956 establishes; this implementing Regulation does not create a separate registration or filing requirement of its own. *Specific registration or filing deadline not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces supporting CBAM-covered importer or customs-broker clients: (1) confirm which default-value set (Annex I, II, III, or IV) applies to the specific goods, indirect emissions, electricity, or unidentified-origin precursor category involved, and (2) flag the scheduled 2027 revision as a trigger to re-confirm the client's default-value basis before that date. *Operational implication:* this is a monitoring-and-advisory step for the forwarder, since the declaration duty itself sits with the importer or authorised CBAM declarant. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

# Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 16 December 2025: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 adopted ("Done at Brussels, 16 December 2025"). In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*
- "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*
- 1 January 2026: application date ("It shall apply from 1 January 2026."). In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*
- 2027: scheduled revision deadline ("It shall be revised in 2027 at the latest"). Future trigger as of the export date. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 of 16 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the establishment of default values, European Commission, OJ, 16 December 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R2621.*

# Sources

entries.body:
# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), the EU regulation harmonising hazard classification and hazard-communication labelling for chemical substances and mixtures placed on the EU market. "The purpose of this Regulation is to ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment as well as the free movement of substances, mixtures and articles... by harmonising the criteria for classification of substances and mixtures, and the rules on labelling and packaging for hazardous substances and mixtures." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

"Manufacturers, importers and downstream users shall classify substances or mixtures in accordance with Title II before placing them on the market." For workspaces that ship, store, or arrange customs clearance for hazardous chemicals, art-restoration or conservation materials, coatings, adhesives, batteries, or other classified substances and mixtures moving through EU supply chains, CLP sets the classification and label content that must appear on the goods and their packaging before EU placement on the market. Critically, "save where Article 33 applies this Regulation shall not apply to the transport of dangerous goods by air, sea, road, rail or inland waterways", meaning the transport leg itself is governed by the UN-based modal dangerous goods rules (ADR, RID, IMDG, IATA-DGR), not by CLP directly. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, in a given transaction, is itself the "manufacturer," "importer," or "downstream user" bearing the CLP classification duty, as opposed to a forwarder arranging carriage of goods someone else has already classified and labelled.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**ACTION REQUIRED.** Confirm dual-labelling compliance on any dangerous-goods shipment with inner and outer packaging, since CLP and the transport dangerous-goods rules apply to different packaging layers at the same time: "Where a package consists of an outer and an inner packaging, together with any intermediate packaging, and the outer packaging meets labelling provisions in accordance with the rules on the transport of dangerous goods, the inner and any intermediate packaging shall be labelled in accordance with this Regulation." *Operational implication:* a shipment can be transport-compliant on its outer packaging (ADR/IMDG/IATA-DGR labelling) while still being CLP-non-compliant on inner packaging if the client or supplier has not applied CLP labels to the inner layer; forwarders should verify both layers, not just the transport documentation, before tendering hazardous cargo. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The CLP classification and labelling duty runs to the manufacturer, importer, or downstream user placing the substance or mixture on the market, and separately "manufacturers, importers and downstream users should re-evaluate the classifications of substances or mixtures they place on the market if they become aware of new adequate and reliable scientific or technical information." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's role (freight forwarder, customs broker, or NVOCC) places it within any of these duty-holder classes for a specific shipment, or whether the duty sits entirely with the shipper or consignee client.

# Substantive Requirements

**General classification obligation.** "Manufacturers, importers and downstream users shall classify substances or mixtures in accordance with Title II before placing them on the market." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**Notification to the Agency.** The Regulation provides "an obligation for manufacturers and importers of substances to notify the Agency of such classifications and label elements if these have not been submitted to the Agency as part of a registration under Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006," and establishes "a classification and labelling inventory of substances." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**Re-evaluation duty.** Manufacturers, importers and downstream users "should re-evaluate the classifications of substances or mixtures they place on the market if they become aware of new adequate and reliable scientific or technical information that may affect those classifications or if they change the composition of their mixtures." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**Advertising restriction.** "Any advertisement for a substance classified as hazardous shall mention the hazard classes or hazard categories concerned." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**Safety data sheet timing.** A safety data sheet "shall be provided free of charge on paper or electronically no later than the date on which the substance or mixture is first supplied." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**Child-resistant fastening.** "Packaging of whatever capacity containing a substance or mixture supplied to the general public and classified for acute toxicity, categories 1 to 3, STOT — single exposure category 1, STOT — repeated exposure category 1, or skin corrosion category 1 shall be fitted with child-resistant fastenings." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**Tactile warning of danger.** "Where the packaging contains a substance or mixture which meets the requirements in section 3.2.1 of Annex II it shall bear a tactile warning of danger in accordance with section 3.2.2 of Annex II." *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**General packaging design duty (Article 35).** "Packaging containing hazardous substances or mixtures shall satisfy the following requirements: (a) the packaging shall be designed and constructed so that its contents cannot escape, except in cases where other more specific safety devices are prescribed;" *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

**Scope of the classification-and-labelling-inventory chapter.** "Article 39 Scope This Chapter shall apply to: (a) substances subject to registration in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006; (b) substances within the scope of Article 1 which meet the criteria for classification as hazardous and are placed on the market either on their own or in a mixture above the concentration limits specified in this Regulation or Directive 1999/45/EC, where relevant" *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

No per-year step-up trajectory is stated in Titles II to IV (Articles 4 to 44); the 1 December 2010/1 June 2015 dates on the Confirmed Regulatory Timeline are two fixed application dates (substances then mixtures), not a multi-step schedule.

Obligations surveyed: 15; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# Exemptions and Edge Cases

"Save where Article 33 applies this Regulation shall not apply to the transport of dangerous goods by air, sea, road, rail or inland waterways." Article 33 itself carves back into scope the inner and intermediate packaging of a shipment even where the outer packaging is governed by the transport dangerous-goods rules: the inner and intermediate packaging "shall be labelled in accordance with this Regulation," and "the outer packaging may also be labelled in accordance with this Regulation." *Operational implication:* the transport exemption is narrower than it first appears; a forwarder cannot treat a shipment as fully outside CLP merely because it is moving under ADR/IMDG/IATA-DGR transport documentation, since inner-packaging CLP labelling remains a live requirement. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

"Member States shall introduce penalties for non-compliance with this Regulation and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that this Regulation is applied. The penalties must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive. Member States shall notify the Commission of the provisions for penalties by 20 June 2010 and shall notify it without delay of any subsequent amendment affecting them." *Analytical inference:* the penalty-setting and notification duties above run to Member States, not to the workspace directly. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.* This is a Member-State-to-Commission notification duty for penalty regimes, not a workspace-facing filing.

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces handling classified substances or mixtures: (1) verify CLP inner-packaging labelling independently of outer-packaging transport compliance on any dangerous-goods shipment, (2) confirm the client or supplier has current classification and label elements, since these must be re-evaluated on new information or a mixture composition change, and (3) confirm safety data sheets are available no later than first supply of the substance or mixture. *Operational implication:* the classification duty itself sits with the manufacturer, importer, or downstream user, but the forwarder's own liability exposure from tendering a mislabelled inner package for carriage is a workspace-facing operational risk. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

# Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**compliance_deadline.** The export's forward-events ledger records two compliance-deadline milestones (each carried twice, at high and medium confidence): "1 December 2010" and "1 June 2015" (the phased substances-then-mixtures application dates for Titles II to IV), and "20 June 2010" (the Member State penalty-notification deadline under Article 47). All three dates are grounded by the primary_deadline and penalty_notification_deadline claims above and appear on the Confirmed Regulatory Timeline. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- "This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." In force as of the export date. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*
- "Titles II, III and IV shall apply in respect of substances from 1 December 2010 and in respect of mixtures from 1 June 2015." In force as of the export date. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*
- 20 June 2010: deadline for Member States to notify the Commission of their penalty provisions under Article 47. In force as of the export date. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*
- 16 December 2008: Regulation adopted ("Done at Strasbourg, 16 December 2008"). In force as of the export date. *Source: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), OJ L 353, 31.12.2008. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272.*
